result.summary:
1) READ the existing regression test in full (test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs:1264-1330). It exercises 2 sibling SUB_PROCESS children (graph_root_split_into_two_subprocesses/1: START -> split(PARALLEL_GATEWAY) -> {sp1, sp2} -> join(PARALLEL_GATEWAY) -> end) both reached via Engine.create/2's own root activation path (design doc iss0396-task-records-multi-sibling-fix.md's own stated actually-reachable trigger, since ISS-0067's guard forecloses reaching this collision via a complete_task/3 hop chain instead). Both children use graph_child_immediate/0 (START->END, no HUMAN_TASK), so both complete synchronously inside Engine.create/2's own transaction.

2) MUTATION TESTING -- 3 targeted mutations against the real shipped fix, each applied, run, observed to fail with real evidence, then reverted and confirmed clean via `git diff` (no residual diff):
   a) Reverted the key_disambiguator argument at sub_process.ex:967-974's TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/7 call (dropped the trailing `parent_token.id` arg, falling back to the pre-fix nil default / fixed {:task_records, instance_id} key). Result: `mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs` -> 15/16 passed, 1 failure -- the ISS-0396 test itself raised `** (RuntimeError) cannot merge Multi; the following operations were found in both Ecto.Multi: [task_records: "<parent_instance_id>"]` at `Engine.create/2` (test line 1287), byte-for-byte the same collision the design doc and ELIXIR-DEV's iteration log describe pre-fix. This is direct, non-speculative proof the test fails against the pre-fix key shape and passes only with the fix.
   b) Reverted load_parent_context/2's join_counters read (sub_process.ex:1133, hardcoded back to `%{}` instead of `SnapshotWriter.deserialize_join_counters(projection.join_counters)`). Result: 15/16 passed, 1 failure -- a DIFFERENT real error, `** (RuntimeError) cannot merge Multi; the following operations were found in both Ecto.Multi: [:execution_error_projection_lock]`, i.e. the join fails with an unknown-branch-id (empty join_counters map) and gets routed into the execution-error path, which itself then collides across siblings -- confirming this fix is load-bearing and distinctly diagnosable from mutation (a).
   c) Reverted reconcile_parent_projection/5's join_counters write-back (sub_process.ex:1289-1295, dropped the `join_counters:` key from `attrs`). Result: 15/16 passed, 1 failure -- `assert parent_projection.status == :completed` failed with `left: :active, right: :completed`: sibling 2's own load_parent_context/2 re-read a stale, pre-sibling-1 join cohort (since sibling 1's cohort update never survived past its own Multi step), so the join never fired and the root instance is left waiting forever. This is a third, distinct failure signature confirming the write-back fix independently from (a) and (b).
   All three mutations were reverted immediately after observation; `git diff lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex` is empty and `mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs` returns to a clean `Result: 16 passed` after each revert and after the final revert.

3) COVERAGE GAP INVESTIGATION -- the existing test's own `all_tasks_for_instance(schema_name, created.instance_id) == []` assertion (line 1318) cannot, on its own, distinguish 'the fixed {:task_records, instance_id, parent_token.id} step ran for both siblings and inserted nothing' from 'the step silently ran for only one sibling and inserted nothing either way', because graph_child_immediate/0's root graph (join -> end directly) never produces a non-empty `final_instance_state.pending_task_nodes` for the ROOT instance at either sibling's own dispatch -- there is nothing for the step to insert regardless of whether it ran once or twice. I attempted to close this by writing a stronger variant (root graph: join -> HUMAN_TASK('after_join') -> end, so the SECOND sibling's own join-firing dispatch would produce a real pending-task entry, letting me assert on an actually-inserted row's existence/count/linkage). This surfaced a genuine, PRE-EXISTING, ISS-0396-UNRELATED defect: TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/7 (by its own docstring/naming) requires every newly-pending token to already be a persisted TokenRecord row, but Transition.dispatch_parallel_join/4 mints a synthetic, non-UUID token id (`"<origin>/join/joined"`, transition.ex:1211) for the freshly-joined branch that has NOT yet been persisted as a TokenRecord at the point this step runs -- `cast_token_record_id/1` (task_activation.ex:326-329) correctly rejects it with `{:error, {:invalid_token_record_id, "<id>/join/joined"}}`. This means 'a SUB_PROCESS-triggered parallel join that continues into further pending work' is not currently a supported code path at all, independent of ISS-0396's fix. This is out of ISS-0396's own stated scope (its design doc and the existing test both only require join -> END with no further work) and fixing it means changing application code (sub_process.ex/task_activation.ex/transition.ex), which is outside TEST-DESIGNER's mandate (test-only). I reverted this exploratory test and its helper graph cleanly -- `git diff --stat test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs` is empty, confirmed via `git status --porcelain` showing a fully clean tree. Given the mutation evidence in (2) already independently and distinctly proves each of the three fixes (key disambiguation, join_counters read, join_counters write-back) is load-bearing and causes a real, differently-shaped failure when reverted, I judge the existing test's coverage of ISS-0396's own acceptance criteria to be adequate as shipped; the join-then-further-work gap is a separate, deeper finding for ORCH to route (new issue), not a defect in this test's coverage of ISS-0396.

4) TEST ISOLATION: confirmed test uses `provisioned_tenant()` (fresh schema per test, per test_developer_guide.md's own DataCase pattern), `active_definition!/2` scoped to that schema_name, `start_attrs/2`'s own `unique_idempotency_key("start")` helper for idempotency-key uniqueness, and `Ecto.UUID.generate()` for actor_id -- no shared mutable state, no wall-clock/unseeded-randomness dependency (DateTime.utc_now() only used for completed_at bookkeeping, never asserted against a fixed value).

5) FINAL VERIFICATION: `mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs` -> `Result: 16 passed`, 0 failures, on the branch exactly as ELIXIR-DEV/REVIEWER left it. No test-code changes were committed (net diff is empty after the revert) since the existing coverage, once verified by mutation, was found adequate for ISS-0396's own scope; a genuine but out-of-scope defect was discovered and is reported below for ORCH rather than silently absorbed into this test.
